`debugger` is a bundled Consuelo OS skill. Coordinates browser evidence, runtime/deployment logs, error tracking, analytics, traces, and code inspection around one observed symptom.

## When to use it

Use this OS skill for runtime debugging across browser behavior, deployment logs, error tracking, analytics, and code evidence. Invoke it for bug triage, incidents, post-merge validation, frontend regressions, worker or queue issues, telephony flows, observability checks, and reconciling runtime truth with code assumptions.

Typical requests include:

- “Find why this worker is failing in production.”
- “Reconcile the browser error with the deployment logs and code.”

## Enable it

```bash
consuelo add skill debugger
```

Run `consuelo add skill` without a name to choose from the skills that are not currently selected. Remove it with:

```bash
consuelo remove skill debugger
```

## What the agent loads

The installed metadata points to `skills/debugger/SKILL.md` in the immutable OS runtime. The compact steering catalog advertises the active skill by name and description; the full `SKILL.md` body is loaded only when the workflow applies.

Metadata for this skill currently declares permission `guidance` and `requiresApproval: no`. Those fields describe the skill contract; individual tools called by the skill still enforce their own authorization and safety rules.

## Boundary

Runtime evidence is the source of truth for observed behavior. Code explains expected behavior; a fix is not proven until the relevant runtime path is verified.

## Verify

After enabling it, confirm `~/Consuelo/Skills/debugger/SKILL.md` exists and that `debugger` appears in `<CONSUELO_HOME>/components/installed-skills.json`. A newly bootstrapped agent should then see `debugger` in the Installed skills portion of steering.
